backendTest.verdict: RED — suite/test COUNTS match the 63/1397 contract exactly (backend source untouched), but exit is 1 on both runs. Every failure is analyzed below; 2 are deterministic stale wave-5 scope guards invalidated by wave 6 landing (backend test files — outside wave-6 unit ownership, need U6R-FIX), 1 was a non-reproducible contention flake.

failures.test: wave-5 client foundation is ON disk; wave-6 feature screens are NOT yet (scope guard — SRS §1.2 / §2.1.2, build-plan §6.1)
failures.analysis: Wave-5-era scope guard that asserts client/src/features/*/routes.jsx does not exist. Wave 6's entire purpose is to create those five feature trees, so the guard's premise expired by design the moment U6-DISCOVERY..U6-ACCOUNT-MOD landed. NOT a product defect; the guard did its job through wave 5 and must now be updated (or retired) by U6R-FIX to assert the wave-6 end-state instead.
failures.disposition: U6R-FIX: update the scope guard to the wave-6 tree (five feature dirs expected present).

failures.test: no non-test client module dereferences a privileged address key unconditionally
failures.analysis: The test's own comment states its premise: 'Wave 5 ships no booking-gated screen, so ANY .addressLine1/.postalCode dereference in shipped client code is premature precision-assumption.' Wave 6 ships exactly that booking-gated screen (ADR-010: pending/in-progress guest sees the exact address). ListingDetailPage.jsx is ADR-010-conformant: it guards with hasPreciseAddress (addressLine1 !== undefined && !== null && !== '') and renders the precise address only when the SERVER's booking-gated serializer included it; the public payload never carries the key. The regex-level blanket ban is what expired, not the invariant.
failures.disposition: U6R-FIX: narrow the guard from 'zero dereferences anywhere' to 'no UNGUARDED dereference / no claim of the key in the public typedef', keeping the ADR-010 direction of the check.

failures.test: AB-08 scraping defenses — listing detail for a STRANGER is the public projection; a pending guest gets the address; a cancelled booking reverts it
failures.analysis: Failed on run 1, PASSED on run 2 of the identical tree, and passes in isolation (npx jest tests/st-security/st-security-wave3.test.js: 50/50, 0.73s vs 5.48s under full-suite contention). Backend source is untouched vs the verified e8a610d baseline. Evidence points to transient cross-worker contention: the suite runs in parallel with tests/rt-lt-resilience/lt-volume-latency.test.js (LT-01: 200 VUs, 145k requests over 45s against the same PostgreSQL server) and a 'terminating connection due to administrator command' idle-pool error is visible in the run-1 log from a resilience suite. A DB-level transient during the stranger GET surfaces as the 500. Flake, not a wave-6 regression.
failures.disposition: Record as flaky-under-contention; candidate hardening for a later wave (retry-once in the test, or serialize the volume-latency suite), NOT a wave-6 blocker.
